content: Real-world reference for a Bitwig <-> external-process bridge: DrivenByMoss OSC extension. It is the canonical proof that a .bwextension can expose the entire project to the outside world over a network socket. Moss's OSC model is bidirectional UDP (Bitwig receives control messages AND sends state-change notifications out), which maps closely onto the bw-brain 'emit events + accept edit primitives' bridge contract. Caveat: OSC/UDP is fire-and-forget with no built-in request/response correlation or delivery guarantee — acceptable for real-time controller feedback, but the WRONG default for reliable patch.apply where an ordered, acknowledged channel is required. Implication for bw-brain: use the OSC pattern as proof-of-capability and for an optional real-time event feed, but choose localhost TCP (newline-delimited JSON) or a stdio relay for the authoritative request/response + apply.patch path.
